author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Apply verified patches and cheats without altering the game image
summary: Match PNACH content to the exact game CRC and serial, preserve the original image, review every effect, test from a clean boot, and remove a patch without contaminating saves.
heroAlt: PCSX2 cheats interface with a list of game-specific toggles

blocks.text: A patch belongs to one executable identity

PCSX2-style patches write to emulated memory when conditions are met. Their filenames and applicability often depend on the game's executable CRC, while region, revision and language variants can move code or data. Keep the verified disc image read-only and load patches externally; modifying the ISO destroys the integrity baseline and makes later troubleshooting ambiguous.
Do not enable an unknown bundle. Read each patch label/source, match CRC and serial, and back up the memory card before testing progression, inventory or unlock cheats.

Record the title, serial, region and CRC reported by EmuCoreX. Obtain the patch from a traceable source with a description of its target revision. Review lines for obvious scope and keep a copy outside the active patches folder. Avoid codes whose only description is 'all cheats' or that request disabling safety features.

items: Verified unmodified personal game image.
Exact serial, region and executable CRC.
Traceable patch source and description.
Cold memory-card backup.
A clean boot without active save state.

blocks.text: Activate the smallest verified patch set

items: 1. Place or import the PNACH through EmuCoreX's patch/cheat manager without opening the disc image in a patcher.
2. Confirm the detected CRC matches the patch identity and disable every optional group initially.
3. Enable one named effect, cold-boot the game and reach the scene where the effect can be observed.
4. Save only after verifying menus, progression and timing; use a separate save slot for cheats that alter inventory or flags.
5. Disable the patch, cold-boot again and confirm the original behaviour returns while the master image hash remains unchanged.

blocks.text: A valid patch logs as matched for the expected CRC, changes only its documented behaviour and can be removed cleanly. Visual patches must be checked across gameplay and FMV; progression cheats must be tested on a disposable save because disabling code cannot always reverse data already written by the game.

items: CRC and serial match the source.
Only selected groups activate.
Original game image hash is unchanged.
Cold boot with patch disabled restores baseline behaviour.
Permanent save changes are isolated in a test slot.

blocks.text: Disable the patch and cold-boot; do not load a state created while it was active as proof of rollback. Restore the backed-up card if the game wrote irreversible flags. Remove the active copy only after the clean boot passes, but retain source/hash notes for diagnosis.

items: Disable all patch groups.
Cold-boot from an in-game save made before the test.
Restore the memory-card backup if progression data changed.
Re-verify the original image hash.
Patch never activates: CRC or revision mismatch.
Wrong values or crash: code targets another executable layout.
Disabling does not undo inventory/progress: game already saved modified data.
Only works from old state: state captured patched memory.

blocks.text: Patches are safest when treated as versioned code: source, target, effect, test and rollback. Keep the original image immutable, activate one purpose at a time and separate cosmetic fixes from cheats that can permanently change a save.
